about: Animal perception and response to a player (TECHNIQUES §35). URL + verbatim quote (≤30 words) per value, or design=true. [EPMC]/[XREF]: abstract read through the Europe PMC / Crossref API. 'not found' items are design values with the direction of the effect sourced where possible.

gray_squirrel.note: Eason et al. 2019, campus and urban parks; pooled

white_tailed_deer.note: that median is for vehicle approaches; no on-foot value found. Design 45 m on foot for a park-like scene (lower in high-visitation parks: Sutton & Heske 2017)

great_blue_heron.quote: A buffer of about 100 m should minimize disturbance to most species of waterbirds we studied in Florida.
great_blue_heron.note: buffers exceed typical flush distances; design FID 60 m

coyote.quote: weakly indicated that rural coyotes would initiate flight at greater distances than urban coyotes
coyote.note: metre values only in a figure

raccoon.quote: They are mostly nocturnal and typically avoid people, though they may be seen during the day while searching for food.

armadillo.quote: armadillos seem oblivious to anything else and may come in close contact to humans before becoming alarmed.

speed_directness.quote: Deer fled at greater distances when approached more quickly and directly

starting_distance.quote: there is a statistical relationship between the distance the human starts walking toward the animal and both the alert distance and the flight initiation distance

start_ratio.quote: Median FID was 40% of start distance, irrespective of start distance or approach speed.
start_ratio.note: vehicle approaches; a check on the model's FID/start-distance ratio, not a law in it

running.quote: The AD and FID were shorter when an individual was walking toward than when he was running toward the focal marmots.

on_foot.quote: Humans on foot were more evocative than other stimuli (vehicles, noises).

crouch.note: no quantified crouching or stopping effect found; a crouched, still player is half as salient

deer_stomp_snort.quote: may stomp its foot, sway its head, and snort.

deer_flag.quote: When startled by danger and fleeing an area whitetails 'flag' their tails as a warning signal.

turkey_putt.quote: The putt is generally associated as an alarm and usually means the bird has seen or heard something and is signaling danger.

squirrel_kuk.quote: rapid kuks and quaas are most often given when a terrestrial predator is around

squirrel_flag.quote: tail flags are elicited by terrestrial threats such as a cat or a human.

armadillo_jump.quote: jump straight into the air, sometimes as high as three or four feet!

turtle_emerge.quote: bold if head emergence latency time was less than or equal to ten seconds
turtle_emerge.note: and 'trials in which individuals did not emerge from their plastron after 600 seconds were terminated.'

deer_fov.quote: distinguish distant objects across a 310 degree field of view

deer_motion.quote: Rods are also better motion sensors than cones.

deer_twilight.quote: deer eyes can detect the best, and are most sensitive, during twilight periods.

turkey_fov.quote: Their field of vision is about 270 degrees

turkey_acuity.quote: three to four times more acute than ours.

armadillo_sight.quote: they often do not notice humans, or other animals, until they are very close.

deer_hearing.quote: At a level of 60 dB sound pressure level, their hearing range extends from 115 Hz to 54 kHz with a best sensitivity of -3 dB at 8 kHz

deer_scent_wind.quote: Keep the wind in your face so that game ahead of you is not spooked by your scent.

wind_cover.quote: When the wind blows you can move, when it stops, so must you.

circle_downwind.quote: many times game will circle downwind if they are suspicious.

scent_distance.note: no peer-reviewed or agency detection distance found

spreading.quote: a sound level drops 6 dB for every doubling of the distance from the source

clap.quote: The loudest configuration, generating an average sound pressure of 85.2 dB
clap.note: distance not stated; taken at 1 m (design)

wind_noise.note: after Bolin 2006 (KTH thesis, Fig. 15 log fits 23–35 log U across sites, Table 1 55.2 dBA at 5.1 m/s; read from the PDF, not quotable as one line). Used as L_wind = 55.2 + 23 log10(U/5.1), floored at 25 dBA

footsteps.note: footstep levels by ground type not found

briggs_D.note: σy for class D (neutral); σz = '.06 x (1 + 0.0015 x ) - .5'. Briggs 1973 open country, stated for 100 m < x < 10 km; used below 100 m as an extrapolation

class_D.quote: D, neutral (heavy overcast day or night)

tolerance.quote: disturbed populations of the three major taxa are more tolerant of human disturbance than less disturbed populations.

deer_vigilance.quote: Deer vigilance was lower in areas with high levels of human recreation, suggesting that deer become habituated

squirrel_exposure.quote: FID increased with starting distance, and it decreased with an increase in human exposure.

hunting.quote: Hunted populations showed significantly greater flight responses than non-hunted populations.

rates.note: per-encounter habituation and sensitisation rates not found

deer_bait.quote: deer concentrate their foraging activities around the baited area.

deer_night.quote: visitation rates of 25:1 night versus day

deer_wariness.quote: This loss of wariness can lead to increased encounters between people and deer

turkey_tame.quote: Feeding, whether direct or indirect, can cause turkeys to act tame

squirrel_peanuts.quote: Squirrels were more likely to take peanuts at locations with more humans and a lower tree density.

raccoon_conditioned.quote: may easily become food conditioned or lose their fear of humans if provided access to food.

walk_speed.note: slow, usual, medium, fast, maximal outdoor paces

proxemics.note: Hall's far social phase; near social '4 to 7 feet (1.2 to 2.1 m)', personal '2.5 to 4 feet (0.76 to 1.22 m)', public '12 to 25 feet (3.7 to 7.6 m)'

greeting.note: Kendon's greeting phases (distance salutation → approach → close salutation); distances not found
